name: blueprint/price-watch
description: Watch a product, flight, or listing price and alert when it crosses a target (Hermes product-price-monitor, righthand-native): a keyless adapter fetches the listing, rh_text_extract pulls the price, the store keeps the history, and rh_notify_send fires once per crossing.
use_cases: tell me when X drops below 200
track a flight price over weeks
ingredients: a keyless adapter per source (blueprint/data-adapter recipe: guardedFetch + normalize + fixture)
rh_text_extract to pull { price, currency, title } out of listing text
rh_store history under price:<slug>:<ts> and the target under price:<slug>:target
rh_notify_send for the crossing alert + a warn-once record
recipe: build the keyless fetcher for the source (recipe: probe -> fixture -> normalize) -> poll: fetch the listing -> rh_text_extract { price, currency } from the page text -> append price:<slug>:<ts> -> compare against price:<slug>:target -> on crossing, rh_notify_send once and record price:<slug>:alerted so the next poll does not re-fire -> history scan doubles as the trend
result_kind: one store record per poll + one alert per threshold crossing

invoke_contract.target: { slug, below: number } -> crossing = latest < below

config_variants.source: keyless listing page | RSS | JSON endpoint (adapter per source)
config_variants.alert: once per crossing | every poll below target

cost_hint: one model call per poll (extract); everything else free
pitfalls: the adapter step is the data-adapter recipe - a source that needs an API token is out of scope
extract answers with a JSON Schema; parse failures are clean errors, not a wrong price
store the target next to the history (same slug) so a poll is one get + one put
warn-once needs its own record or every poll below target re-notifies
prices as numbers, times as ISO strings - JSON-serializable only
anti-bot walls are the real risk: probe the source first and record the UA/cookie requirements in the adapter's LEARNINGS
local_limits: polls only run when the agent runs - no server-side scheduler
cloud_limits: cron escalation (documented) needs a Worker; same shape as reminder-flow/heartbeat
